title: Restriction of the specified diagonal factors and integration adjunct to a bundle frame
statement:
Fix [def-pur-conventions] with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $S$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme, without absolute separatedness, and $\pi:V\to S$ a vector bundle of rank $d\geq0$ with zero section [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Use small pro-etale derived pullback, constructible exceptional inverse image and the specified Tate twists [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Put $\omega_\pi=R\pi^!\Lambda_S$, let $\vartheta_\pi:\omega_\pi\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_V(d)[2d]$ be the glued diagonal orientation [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object], and let $P_\pi:\Lambda_V(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_\pi$ be the exceptional transpose of the actual integration of [def-amb-vector-integration], realized by [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison, cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity].

Let $u:U\hookrightarrow S$ be an affine open finite type over $k$ with a chosen linear frame $\phi:V_U\xrightarrow{\sim}X=\mathbf A^d_U$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. Write $j:V_U\hookrightarrow V$, $p:X\to U$, and $\rho:Lj^*\omega_\pi\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_p$ for the exceptional open-base-change comparison followed by $\phi$. Write $\tau:Lj^*(\Lambda_V(d)[2d])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ for the specified Tate restriction and frame identification. On $W=X\times_UX$ let $p_1,p_2$ be the projections and $\Delta$ the diagonal, let $N=N_{\Delta/W}$ have projection $\pi_N:N\to X$ and zero section $z_N$ [def-pur-normal-bundle], and write $C(g,s)=Ls^*Rg^!\Lambda$ [def-pur-section-invariant]. Set $\alpha:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_p$ equal to the diagonal base-change comparison [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], $\delta:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\pi_N,z_N)$ equal to normalized DNC [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], and $\beta:C(\pi_N,z_N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ equal to $Lz_N^*(P_{\pi_N}^{-1})$ followed by Tate restriction. Here $P_{\pi_N}$ is the actual integration adjunct, with the same site comparison as $P_\pi$. Let $P_p$ denote the corresponding actual integration adjunct for $p$. Then the two restriction formulas, as equalities of derived morphisms, are
$$\tau\circ Lj^*\vartheta_\pi\circ\rho^{-1}=\beta\circ\delta\circ\alpha^{-1},\qquad
\rho\circ Lj^*P_\pi\circ\tau^{-1}=P_p.$$
The first formula uses exactly the diagonal/DNC normalization specified in [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement]. Each of its three factors commutes with further affine target-open restriction under the canonical pullback-composition, normalized DNC, and integration-normalized zero-section comparisons, respectively. In the source identification for $\alpha$, the equality $p_2\Delta=1$ has its canonical pullback-composition comparison. Both displayed formulas commute with further restriction of the chosen frame and with change of frame through an isomorphism over $U$, using the canonical exceptional-adjunction and Tate comparisons. For two target frames these comparisons agree on affine refinements of their intersection, without requiring that intersection affine. The formulas include empty $U$ and rank zero. No equality between the diagonal orientation and inverse integration adjunct is assumed in these assertions.

proof.text: The geometric domains do not require absolute separatedness of $S$. By [lem-pur-vector-bundle-finite-type-frames], $\pi$ is separated finite type and smooth of pure relative dimension $d$, and $S,V$ are Noetherian. For the given frame, $V_U\cong X=\mathbf A^d_U$ is affine and separated finite type over $k$. Applying [lem-pur-affine-target-diagonal-dnc] to $f=\pi$ and the affine target $U$ gives the restriction $\rho$ before the frame identification, the separated finite-type diagonal pair, and its rank-$d$ normal bundle. Thus every DNC application below takes place over $X$, a separated scheme, and never over the possibly nonseparated global $V$. The coefficient stage is exactly $A_{\mathbf Q_\ell,n}=\Lambda$ with $n\geq1$.

proof.text:
Apply the first displayed restriction formula of [lem-pur-diagonal-dnc-chart-normalization] to $f=\pi$, target chart $U\subseteq S$ and source chart $V_U\subseteq V$. The latter is affine by Step 1. Its $h$ is $\pi_U$, and its $\alpha_h,\delta_h,\beta_h$ are the diagonal, normalized DNC and zero-section inverse-purity arrows. Identify this entire diagram with the one for $p$ by $\phi$. The root-projection and transpose comparisons of [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] identify its integration-normalized $\beta_h$ with the specified $Lz_N^*(P_{\pi_N}^{-1})$ followed by Tate restriction. Consequently the chart formula is precisely
$$\tau\circ Lj^*\vartheta_\pi\circ\rho^{-1}=\beta\circ\delta\circ\alpha^{-1}.$$
This uses only the diagonal assembly clause of the chart-normalization node, not its later comparison with ordered affine purity.

proof.text:
Apply the base-change equation of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] to $K=\Lambda_S$ and $u:U\hookrightarrow S$. Its $\gamma_{\pi,K}$ is the adjoint of the actual integration and hence is $P_\pi$; its tensor/pullback/Tate associator at the unit is $\tau$, and its exceptional exchange is $\rho$, after the frame identification. The transpose identity $P=C_V(\eta^e)$ of [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison], applied over $S$ and over $U$, identifies both integration adjuncts with the comparison images of the etale ones. The exchange is identified separately: [lem-pur-bounded-site-exchange-transposes], which assumes no absolute separatedness, applied to $f=\pi$, $v=u$ and $K=A_S$, gives $a_{\pi_U,A_U}\circ C_{V_U}(d^e)=d^p\circ Lj^*(a_{\pi,A_S})$, where $d^p$ is the dualizing base-change arrow of [def-pur-co-smoothness], i.e. $\rho$ before the frame identification, and $a$ is the site comparison $C\,\pi^{\times,e}\cong R\pi^!C$ used in the transpose identity. Applying $C_{V_U}$ to the etale equation and conjugating by these comparisons, with the canonical pullback identifications of the twists, therefore carries this same equation to the specified pro-etale one, also when $S$ is not separated. The resulting equation is
$$\rho\circ Lj^*P_\pi=P_p\circ\tau.$$
Compose on the right with $\tau^{-1}$ to obtain the second formula. Neither this argument nor Step 2 equates $\vartheta_\pi$ with $P_\pi^{-1}$.

proof.text: For a further finite-type affine target open $U'\subseteq U$, [lem-pur-diagonal-orientation-refinement] identifies the restricted diagonal pair and normal bundle with those for $\pi_{U'}$, and states separately that $\rho,\alpha,\delta,\beta$ restrict to the corresponding four arrows. This includes the specified integration-normalized zero-section comparison, by the site identification of Step 2. The equation for $P$ in Step 3 applies to the composite target inclusion as well. The exceptional comparisons for two inclusions compose by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], since they are mates of the pasted compact-support squares. In $\alpha$, the arrow $L\Delta^*Lp_2^*\omega_p\cong L(p_2\Delta)^*\omega_p\cong\omega_p$ is the inverse of the compositor of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], followed by the identity comparison; no independently chosen trivialization is used. The Tate arrows are those of [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists]. Applying pullback to the two displayed composites therefore gives their versions for $U'$, with the canonical composition comparisons.

source.place: Step 3: compatibility of the diagonal base change, normalized DNC and final vector-bundle purity arrows; affine-frame restriction and change-of-frame bookkeeping

proof.text: Consider two linear frames over $U$, with change $a:\mathbf A^d_U\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf A^d_U$, $x\mapsto Gx$, $G\in\mathrm{GL}_d(\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U))$. The isomorphism $a\times a$ sends $\Delta$ to $\Delta$ and commutes with both projections over $a$. The diagonal base-change square for one frame is therefore isomorphic to that for the other; [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies their exceptional mates, including the pullback-composition arrow in Step 4. For the normal map, write the diagonal ideal in affine coordinates as $(v_1,\ldots,v_d)$ with $v=y-x$. Then $a(y)-a(x)=Gv$; on every quotient $\mathcal I^r/\mathcal I^{r+1}$ the map is the degree-$r$ substitution induced by $v\mapsto Gv$. The normal-cone definition [def-pur-normal-bundle] thus gives the same linear normal coordinate change $G$, preserving its zero section. In centred coordinates both DNC comparisons are the identity on the standard section invariant. Conjugating the identity by this same coordinate change on its two sides leaves the identity. The uniqueness and etale compatibility of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] identify the transported comparison with $\delta$ in the new frame. This proves the required compatibility of $\alpha$ and $\delta$ under frame change.

source.place: Step 3: compatibility of the diagonal base change, normalized DNC and final vector-bundle purity arrows; affine-frame restriction and change-of-frame bookkeeping

proof.text: For the last factor and for $P_p$, use integration, independently of any diagonal orientation. The actual affine trace satisfies $t_p\circ\rho_G=t_p$ by [lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance], with $N=\ell^n$ and $A=\Lambda$. Its hypotheses hold on $U$, and also on $X$ for the normal bundle: these schemes are Noetherian, $\ell$ is invertible, $\ell^nA=0$, and the normal coordinate change of Step 5 is linear after the base identification $a$. [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] carries these actual trace equalities and their adjoint transposes to the specified pro-etale twists. More explicitly, on these separated charts [lem-pur-trace-transpose-base-change] says that the transpose of a transported trace is the exceptional mate composed with the pulled-back transpose. A Cartesian square with top arrow an isomorphism is obtained from the identity pullback square by that isomorphism; [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] supplies exactly its canonical mate. Thus the trace equalities imply equivariance of $P_p$ and of $P_{\pi_N}$. Invert the latter equation and pull it back along the equivariant zero section; the canonical Tate comparison gives equivariance of $\beta$. Together with Step 5, this proves frame-change compatibility of both formulas, using exactly the diagonal/DNC and integration normalization in the statement.

source.place: Step 3: compatibility of the diagonal base change, normalized DNC and final vector-bundle purity arrows; affine-frame restriction and change-of-frame bookkeeping

proof.text: For target frames on $U_1,U_2$, [lem-pur-vector-bundle-finite-type-frames] supplies finite-type affine refinements $T\subseteq U_1\cap U_2$. On each $T$, Step 4 restricts both diagrams to their $T$-diagrams and Steps 5--6 compare their two linear frames; pasting the same canonical comparisons gives agreement on every further refinement. This proves exactly the overlap assertion without assuming $U_1\cap U_2$ affine or inferring descent for arbitrary derived morphisms. If $U$ is empty, every diagram lives in the zero category, so its arrows and equalities are unique. If $d=0$, the bundle and frame are identities by [lem-pur-vector-bundle-finite-type-frames]; the chart-normalization node includes the identity diagonal/DNC data, and [def-amb-vector-integration] specifies the identity adjunction trace. Its transpose is the identity, so both formulas reduce to identities. These checks impose no extra hypotheses.
